pathSubtitle: Communicate health concerns, describe symptoms, and understand medical advice clearly.

lessons.title: Describing Basic Symptoms
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Describing Basic Symptoms successfully

questions.prompt: How long has the patient had symptoms?
options: One day
Three days
A week
questions.feedback: Correct! The patient has had symptoms for three days.

questions.prompt: What does the doctor ask the patient to do?
options: Lie down
Open their mouth
Breathe deeply
questions.feedback: Correct! The doctor asks the patient to open their mouth.

questions.prompt: What does "symptom" mean?
options: a painful or irritated feeling in the throat
a pain inside the head
a sign of illness felt by a patient
questions.feedback: Correct! "symptom" means a sign of illness felt by a patient.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "sore throat"?
options: A sore throat is a common symptom of a cold.
I've had a headache all day.
I have a bad sore throat and can't swallow.
questions.feedback: Correct! "I have a bad sore throat and can't swallow." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "headache" mean?
options: a sign of illness felt by a patient
a painful or irritated feeling in the throat
a pain inside the head
questions.feedback: Correct! "headache" means a pain inside the head.

lessons.title: Getting a Prescription
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Getting a Prescription successfully

questions.prompt: What type of infection does the patient have?
options: Viral
Bacterial
Fungal
questions.feedback: Correct! The patient has a bacterial infection.

questions.prompt: What should the patient do if they get a rash?
options: Take more medicine
Stop and return to the doctor
Drink more water
questions.feedback: Correct! The patient should stop and return to the doctor.

questions.prompt: What does "prescribe" mean?
options: medicines that kill bacterial infections
an unwanted result of taking a medication
to officially tell a patient to take a medicine
questions.feedback: Correct! "prescribe" means to officially tell a patient to take a medicine.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "antibiotics"?
options: The doctor prescribed antibiotics for the infection.
One side effect of this medicine is dizziness.
Always finish your course of antibiotics.
questions.feedback: Correct! "Always finish your course of antibiotics." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "side effect" mean?
options: to officially tell a patient to take a medicine
medicines that kill bacterial infections
an unwanted result of taking a medication
questions.feedback: Correct! "side effect" means an unwanted result of taking a medication.

lessons.title: Describing Pain
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Describing Pain successfully

questions.prompt: What caused the back pain?
options: A car accident
Moving heavy boxes
A sports injury
questions.feedback: Correct! The back pain started after moving heavy boxes.

questions.prompt: Where does the tingling feeling go?
options: Up the back
Down the right leg
Into the left arm
questions.feedback: Correct! The tingling goes down the right leg.

questions.prompt: What does "sharp" mean?
options: a continuous, low-level pain that is not intense
happening all the time without stopping
a sudden, intense pain (like a knife)
questions.feedback: Correct! "sharp" means a sudden, intense pain (like a knife).

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "dull ache"?
options: I feel a sharp pain when I breathe in.
The pain is constant — it never goes away.
I have a dull ache in my shoulder.
questions.feedback: Correct! "I have a dull ache in my shoulder." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "constant" mean?
options: a sudden, intense pain (like a knife)
a continuous, low-level pain that is not intense
happening all the time without stopping
questions.feedback: Correct! "constant" means happening all the time without stopping.

lessons.title: Mental Health Consultation
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Mental Health Consultation successfully

questions.prompt: Which symptom does the patient NOT mention?
options: Poor sleep
Chest pain
Loss of interest
questions.feedback: Correct! The patient does not mention chest pain.

questions.prompt: What significant life change happened six months ago?
options: They moved house
They changed jobs
They ended a relationship
questions.feedback: Correct! The patient changed jobs six months ago.

questions.prompt: What does "exhausted" mean?
options: continuing for a long time; not stopping
severe and sudden in onset (in medical terms)
extremely tired, with no energy left
questions.feedback: Correct! "exhausted" means extremely tired, with no energy left.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "persistent"?
options: I feel completely exhausted, even after a full night's sleep.
The patient arrived with acute chest pain.
She has a persistent cough that won't go away.
questions.feedback: Correct! "She has a persistent cough that won't go away." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "acute" mean?
options: extremely tired, with no energy left
continuing for a long time; not stopping
severe and sudden in onset (in medical terms)
questions.feedback: Correct! "acute" means severe and sudden in onset (in medical terms).

lessons.title: Specialist Referral & Second Opinion
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Specialist Referral & Second Opinion successfully

questions.prompt: Why is the doctor referring the patient?
options: Broken bone
ECG irregularities
High blood pressure
questions.feedback: Correct! The doctor is referring the patient due to ECG irregularities.

questions.prompt: What does the doctor say about seeking a second opinion?
options: It's not advisable
It's the patient's right
It will delay treatment
questions.feedback: Correct! The doctor says a second opinion is the patient's right.

questions.prompt: What does "referral" mean?
options: a doctor who specialises in the heart
something that is irregular or unexpected
when a doctor sends a patient to see a specialist
questions.feedback: Correct! "referral" means when a doctor sends a patient to see a specialist.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "cardiologist"?
options: I have a referral to see a specialist next month.
The scan revealed a small anomaly.
The cardiologist reviewed my ECG results.
questions.feedback: Correct! "The cardiologist reviewed my ECG results." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "anomaly" mean?
options: when a doctor sends a patient to see a specialist
a doctor who specialises in the heart
something that is irregular or unexpected
questions.feedback: Correct! "anomaly" means something that is irregular or unexpected.
